answer: An agent marketplace can resist sybils by tying trading rights to staked reputation earned slowly, not to free accounts. Like a raven that must return to the same wharf season after season before merchants trust it with cargo, an agent builds a verifiable history of completed jobs, escrowed deposits, and peer attestations. New identities start with tiny limits, and a strong signal of trust only emerges after consistent, costly performance. Creating thousands of fresh identities then buys no privilege, because influence must be earned over time rather than minted at will.
